feature_notes: The window is chromeless by composition: transparent titlebar, hidden title, clear non-opaque background, no titlebar separator (the comment says a focused window's separator would cut through the rounded corner), shadow kept on, and background dragging disabled
configure(_:) is idempotent through a weak NSHashTable because viewDidMoveToWindow fires on every reorder, so the setup pays once per window

autorecalculatesKeyViewLoop = true is a deliberate fix, not a default: with it on, SwiftUI only marks the loop dirty and keeps its focus items by the finite group-based route, and nothing is rebuilt during layout

Traffic lights are never animated mid-live-resize because a fresh animation group every frame made them lag behind the window; they follow unanimated and a final unanimated placement plus fitTitlebar runs on NSWindow.didEndLiveResizeNotification
Traffic lights are also placed unanimated while the sidebar edge is being dragged (sidebarDragging = true), so they track the drag exactly
fitTitlebar only ever grows the container (guard fitted.height < titlebarHeight) and keeps the top edge fixed; in an unflipped theme frame it sets origin.y = maxY - titlebarHeight

titlebarFrameDidChange coalesces work: it queues nothing if the container already has at least titlebarHeight or a fit is already pending, and the queued fit is a frame assignment only, never a synchronous layout or draw
WindowChromeProbeView.hitTest returns nil, so the probe view never intercepts mouse events
The first placement on entering a window is unanimated (animated: false)

Sidebar collapse by drag: releasing below collapseThreshold 110 hides the sidebar with Chrome.panelSlide and snaps width back to restingWidth; otherwise the width settles at max(minimumWidth, width), becomes the new restingWidth and springs there with Chrome.panelSlide. Either way persist() runs and isDragging clears

beginDrag() from a hidden sidebar sets width = 0 and isVisible = true inside a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true, so the sidebar can be dragged out from the edge with no jump; from a visible sidebar it just anchors at the current width
drag(by:) clamps to 0...maximumWidth, so the lower bound during a drag is 0 rather than minimumWidth and the edge can be pulled past the collapse point

toggle() opens from restingWidth and starts a slide whose slideDelta is -restingWidth when opening and +width when closing; the chat pane uses slideDelta and isSliding to treat the slide as one pane reshape with a single layout width rather than a spring
isSliding is cleared by a cancellable task after slideRun ms (420, or 220 with Reduce Motion), the point at which Chrome.panelSlide's spring is judged visually settled

holdsTrafficLights flips from the width actually laid out each frame via noteLaidOutWidth, not from the target state, so the buttons move into the sidebar's corner only once it is genuinely wide enough and the chrome closes up at the same moment; unchanged widths write no state, and lastLaidOutWidth starts at -1 so the first report always lands
renderedWidth is width when visible and 0 when hidden

The resize strip refreshes hover from the real cursor position (window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream converted into view space) in layout(), viewDidMoveToWindow() and on mouseUp, because a toggle or a spring-back can carry the strip out from under a resting cursor and AppKit only reports enter and exit for mouse movement; layout() animates the grip only when that recheck actually changed isHovering
The strip refuses window dragging (mouseDownCanMoveWindow = false) even though its top runs through the stretched titlebar, and accepts first mouse so an inactive window can be resized in one click
When isActive is false the strip has no cursor rect, no hover and hitTest returns nil, so it is fully inert; showsGrip is isActive && (isHovering || isDragging)
The tracking area is rebuilt in updateTrackingAreas with rect .zero and options [.mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeAlways, .inVisibleRect]
Drag deltas are reported as event.locationInWindow.x - pressOriginX, with the final delta sent once more on mouseUp before onEnd, and the grip animates on both mouseDown and mouseUp

purpose: The Metal stitchable distortion shader that reproduces the macOS Dock genie effect for archived rows: it maps each destination pixel back into the flying row's frame through a fixed funnel whose sides bend from the row's width down to a narrow neck at the target point.
key_symbols: [[ stitchable ]] float2 genie(float2 position, float progress, float4 source, float2 target)
locals: t, pinch, slide, width, height, flip, x0, y0, targetY, positionY, travel, depth, bend, neck, left, right, u, sourceY
calls_into: Invoked from Swift as ShaderLibrary.genie(.float(progress), .float4(x, y, w, h), .float2(target.x, target.y)) in Genie.swift
platform_assumptions: Metal Shading Language compiled into the app's default shader library
SwiftUI's [[stitchable]] distortionEffect convention: the function receives a destination position and returns the source position to sample
feature_notes: progress is animation progress 0...1, explicitly never a clock; source is the row's frame (x, y, width, height) and target the neck, both in the layer's coordinates
pinch = smoothstep(0.0, 0.45, t) controls how far the sides have bent in; slide = smoothstep(0.2, 1.0, t) controls how far the row has travelled
flip = 1.0 when target.y >= source.y + height * 0.5, else -1.0; the vertical axis is mirrored on the way in and out so a target above the row funnels upwards
travel = max(targetY - y0, height); depth = clamp((positionY - y0) / travel, 0, 1); bend = pinch * smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, depth)
neck = min(24.0, width): the funnel's narrow end is at most 24 points wide
left = mix(x0, target.x - neck * 0.5, bend), right = mix(x0 + width, target.x + neck * 0.5, bend), u = (position.x - left) / max(right - left, 0.0001)

Three discard conditions return 'nothing' (-100000, -100000), sampling nothing: positionY > targetY (past the neck), u outside [0, 1] (outside the funnel), and sourceY outside [y0, y0 + height] (past the row)
sourceY = positionY - slide * (targetY - y0); the returned sample is float2(x0 + u * width, flip * sourceY)

purpose: A tiny additive-synthesis engine that renders struck-bell tones to a complete 16-bit mono PCM WAV byte buffer in memory, including hand-written RIFF header emission, so the app's chimes are numbers in source rather than bundled audio assets.
key_symbols: struct ToneSynth.Note { var frequency: Double; var onset: Double; var level: Double }
struct ToneSynth.Partial { var multiple: Double; var level: Double; var decay: Double }
static func wave(notes: [Note], partials: [Partial], duration: Double) -> Data
local generic func append<Value: FixedWidthInteger>(_ value: Value) inside wave
calls_into: cos, sin, exp, abs from the C math library
state_owned: No instance state; only the private static constants sampleRate, attack, release. wave() allocates a local [Double] sample buffer of Int(sampleRate * duration) elements.
side_effects: Pure computation - allocates and returns Data; no I/O, no timers, no notifications
platform_assumptions: Foundation only (import Foundation); no AppKit dependency, so the synthesis itself is portable
Assumes the consumer (NSSound on macOS) can play a raw RIFF/WAVE buffer from memory
Little-endian byte order is written explicitly via .littleEndian, so it is not host-endianness dependent
feature_notes: Sample rate 44_100.0 Hz, mono, 16-bit signed PCM.
Sample count = Int(sampleRate * duration).
Attack: raised-cosine onset of 0.006 s - for time < attack the envelope is 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(.pi * time / attack), else 1. 'quick enough to feel struck, with no click.'
Release: final 0.08 s linear fade, applied as samples[index] *= Double(count - index) / Double(fade) over indices (count - fade)..<count.

Per-note synthesis: start index = Int(note.onset * sampleRate); time = Double(index - start) / sampleRate; tone = sum over partials of partial.level * exp(-time / partial.decay) * sin(2 * .pi * note.frequency * partial.multiple * time); accumulated as samples[index] += note.level * onset * tone.
Partial.decay is documented as 'the seconds it takes to fall by about two thirds' (an exp(-t/decay) time constant).
Normalization: peak = max abs sample; scale = peak > 0 ? 0.9 / peak : 0 - every rendered tone is normalized to 0.9 full scale.

WAV header written by hand, in order: ASCII 'RIFF'; UInt32(36 + count * 2); 'WAVE'; 'fmt '; UInt32(16); UInt16(1) // PCM; UInt16(1) // mono; UInt32(sampleRate); UInt32(sampleRate) * 2 // bytes per second; UInt16(2) // bytes per frame; UInt16(16) // bits per sample; 'data'; UInt32(count * 2); then Int16 samples.
Data is preallocated with capacity 44 + count * 2 (44-byte canonical WAV header).
Sample conversion: Int16((sample * scale * Double(Int16.max)).rounded()).
Shipped and reachable: the only callers are FinishChime and SettleChime in this same bundle.
unresolved_questions: A note whose onset is at or beyond duration would make start >= count and the range start..<count invalid (a crash); no guard exists. Both shipped callers use onsets (0.14 s, 0.075 s) far below their durations, so this is unreachable in practice but unverified as intentional.

feature_notes: Guidance is ON by default; turning the switch off does not merely omit the block, it sends a matching 'off' block that 'tells the model to disregard the earlier app-provided guidance and to keep following user requests and project requirements'

The guidance asks for: the shortest complete answer, leading with the result, skipping filler and hype, comments only where they explain a non-obvious reason, focused edits instead of unrelated cleanup, product-fitting UI structure, and reusing evidence rather than re-reading it
Delivery timing: 'The setting takes effect on the next message.' A message already in flight is not changed; toggling does not rewrite the current conversation or thread history

Delivery per provider class: providers with system-instruction support receive it when their session starts or resumes; other providers receive it with the first ordinary message of a session and again after explicit compaction; slash commands defer delivery until that ordinary message; automatic history changes inside those providers are not observable by the app
Explicit non-promise: 'Nothing is promised about token savings.' No fixed saving is guaranteed and no such claim is made in the UI

Coverage: the block is attached to the provider request so it reaches every provider Droppy Code runs; Hydra heads are covered because the block itself asks that the guidance apply to delegated work, with the intent that a head answers under the same policy as its lead

Attribution: upstream inspiration is miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop at revision 743735248fbaefd76bb56619615687dfa8b3bc1e, MIT licensed, copyright 2026 Miqdad Badjuber; the upstream LICENSE applies to that work

Intentionally left out of Droppy Code, as a three-item bulleted list: 'The upstream wizard and its interactive setup.', 'Mandatory audit reports.', 'External executables or scripts the upstream project may invoke.'

Warning line on stderr: 'Warning: !{iid} ({title}) is not mentioned in the Thanks section.'
'Missing from the Thanks section:' header followed by one suggested line per missing contributor
'No outside contributors since {tag}.' on stderr, or '[]' with --json

commits_in_range uses git log --no-merges with format %H%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%s%x1f%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly), splitting on \x1f and padding to 5 fields
COAUTHOR_RE = (.+?)\s*<([^<>]+)>\s* parses each Co-authored-by trailer into name and email
merged_requests matches MRs by squash_commit_sha, merge_commit_sha or sha against the range's shas, falling back to merged_in() which tests ancestry against HEAD and origin/main but not the tag

MAINTAINER_USERNAMES filtering drops the maintainer's own MRs; ignored_email drops maintainer emails and anything ending in @anthropic.com, @users.noreply.github.com or @localhost, so Claude co-author trailers and GitHub noreply addresses never appear
Commit subjects are only recorded for commits NOT linked to a matched MR, so an MR contributor is credited by title and a direct committer by subject
Email entries are folded into a user entry when the display names match case-insensitively
Entries sort by lowest MR iid (MR-less entries last, float('inf')) then by lowercased name; each entry's mrs sort by iid

check_notes finds the section under a line whose strip() is exactly '## Thanks' or '### Thanks' and stops at the next line starting with '#'; a contributor counts as named if '@handle' or the name appears case-insensitively in it
CLI: --since <tag> / --since=<tag>, --json, --check <file> / --check=<file>; anything else prints 'Unknown argument: {arg}' to stderr and returns 2
--check returns 0 immediately when there are no outside contributors at all
unresolved_questions: check_notes takes a `tag` parameter it never uses.
When glab is missing or the API call fails, merged_requests silently returns [] and credits degrade to commit-based entries with no visible warning.

encode_film runs ffmpeg twice per film: libx264 -preset slow -crf 19 -profile:v high -level 5.1 -g 120, and hevc_videotoolbox -b:v <bitrate> -tag:v hvc1 -g 120; common flags are -vf scale='min(<width>,iw)':-2:flags=lanczos -r 60 -fps_mode cfr -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -an plus the master's own -color_primaries/-color_trc/-colorspace when not 'unknown'
The poster is the film's own first frame, extracted with -frames:v 1 and encoded as <name>-poster.webp

pane_crop finds the chat pane by diffing against blank-wide.png inside the box (684, 244, 2764, 1624), thresholding a difference above 18 to 255, taking getbbox, moving 40 px above the first content and running to (2764, 1864)

wait_for_run first waits the app into existence (60 tries, 2 s apart, because a fresh bundle's first launch can take a minute to clear LaunchServices) and exits 'the run never launched (<marker>)' if it never appears
capture() exits 'The capture run wrote no <master> film; see <log>' when a film is missing or zero bytes; capture_tour() lists every missing still in one message
ffprobe reads width, height, avg_frame_rate, color_space, color_transfer, color_primaries and color_range from stream v:0 as JSON

CLI: no flags means build + capture_tour + encode_tour; --website adds the wallpaper capture/encode/upload path; --encode skips build and capture; --upload-only skips build, capture and encode; --upload or --upload-only uploads

feature_notes: The header comment lists everything deliberately DROPPED from Droppy's original changelog styles because there is nothing to wear them on this page: the frame-sequence hero (.changelog-scrub), the light-paper hero ink override, the nightly/beta/iOS/playground/droppykit channel variants and the .is-nightly/.is-beta/.is-ios rules, the channel note, entry actions, TestFlight, galleries, video, image, lightbox, whatsnew label, and the per-platform float-icon faces. Only the stable channel ships.

Release entries are a two-column grid: the left column (date plus display title) pins with position: sticky at top 108px while the right column's notes scroll past, 'like a product-blog changelog' per the comment.

Stable pill animation: two absolutely positioned overlay layers that only ever change opacity, running on two different periods (5.4s and 7.1s) 'so the pill breathes unevenly rather than pulsing in unison'. channel-breathe-a goes 0.55 at 0%/100% and 1 at 50%; channel-breathe-b goes 1 at 0%/100% and 0.5 at 50%.

Stable droplet streams: ::before background-image is radial-gradient(circle at 7px 4px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.90) 0 0.8px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 2px) plus radial-gradient(circle at 14px 13px, rgba(219, 231, 255, 0.75) 0 0.6px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 1.6px), background-size 20px 20px, animation stable-drizzle-a 4.2s linear infinite. ::after is radial-gradient(circle at 4px 12px, rgba(219, 231, 255, 0.80) 0 0.7px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 1.8px) plus radial-gradient(circle at 16px 5px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.70) 0 1px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0) 2.3px), background-size 24px 24px, background-position 8px 0, animation stable-drizzle-b 5.4s linear infinite.

Seamlessness rule: each drizzle keyframe scrolls its repeating tile by exactly one tile height downward, in px so a seam is impossible at any rounding. stable-drizzle-a goes from background-position 0 -20px to 0 0; stable-drizzle-b goes from 8px -24px to 8px 0. Comment: 'the loop is seamless and no droplet ever pops or respawns'.

prefers-reduced-motion: reduce kills both pill overlay animations and pins them at opacity 0.9, and flattens .clog-float-icon__face to scale(var(--face-scale, 1)) with filter none and a 320ms opacity-only transition, keeping the dissolve and dropping the movement.
The marker dot takes its channel's colour, #1e40af for stable, 'so the row reads as one thing'.

Comment on .changelog-entry__version: the headline above is the human name for the release, the version is the exact build string kept for support and bug reports, 'the thing you paste into a post', so it stays literal and stays quiet.
Comment: stable is royal blue on purpose because it is the tier the download button gives you.

The single .clog-float-icon carries only one face, the Droppy Code artwork; it cross-dissolves with a little scale and blur on hand-off between entries so the icon reads as gliding down the page rather than being swapped.

The comment for .scrub-frost says Droppy's halo is paper-coloured for its light art, while here it is canvas-coloured (rgba(11, 14, 20, ...) matches --bg-top #0b0e14) for the dark page, and one class on the copy group covers kicker, title and subtitle at once.
unresolved_questions: The markup that pairs with these classes lives in website/changelog.html, which is not in this bundle, so the exact user-visible strings for .changelog-state__title, .changelog-state__text and the .changelog-more toggle label cannot be determined from this file.
--face-scale is consumed with fallback 1 but never declared here; the script that positions .clog-float-icon must set it per face, and that script is not in this bundle.

.changelog-entry.is-stable is the only channel state class kept, but whether the page script can still emit other is-* channel classes (which would then fall through to the :root defaults) cannot be established from CSS alone.

.scrub-frost's exclusion selector references .e2ee and .board-tools; neither class is defined in this file or in site.css, so they look like leftovers from the upstream Droppy page, but that cannot be confirmed from this bundle.
.changelog-hero .hero__kicker-mark sets filter: none to undo a recolor, but the original filter is not in this file (it lived in Droppy's inline block), so what it undid is not recoverable here.

purpose: The single shared design system stylesheet for the whole Droppy Code marketing site. Header comment: 'A dark port of the getdroppy.app design system: the same notch dock, pills, reveal motion, highlight rail, FAQ and footer, re-tokened for a deep code-editor canvas and the blue of the Droppy Code icon. The binary field and the tile system are new and live at the bottom.' It declares every design token, the reset, the site-wide anti-copy lockdown, the fixed notch nav with its spring-open intro, the button morph-hover system, the hero with its animated charged word and binary canvas field, feature cards, the horizontal highlight rail, the tile card system, agent marks, usage limits, stats, the free and open-source card that takes the pricing slot, the zig-zag FAQ accordion, the outro, the footer with its giant wordmark, and the theme picker plus binary twinkles. Explicitly no build step, one stylesheet, one page.
key_symbols: :root token block (colors, radii, fonts, type scale, container, nav geometry, easings, durations)

Reset: *, *::before, *::after; html; body (declared twice, second rule adds the anti-copy lockdown); img, video (twice); a; button; h1,h2,h3,h4,p; ul,ol; code,kbd,pre; ::selection; :where(a,button,input,select,textarea,[tabindex]):focus-visible; .nav :focus-visible
second :root block with --nav-dock-* tokens; @keyframes navDockExpand; html.nav-intro-done .nav__pill

site.js builds the two .btn-morph__face layers at runtime 'so button markup stays plain', and toggles .is-tapmorph, .is-open (nav pill and FAQ item), .is-visible and .is-settled (reveal), .is-dragging (highlight rail), .is-current (theme stage image and name), .is-active (nav link)
A head-inline gate script adds html.nav-intro-done on later loads so the nav dock intro never replays between pages
Canvas elements inside .hero__field and .outro__field, driven by the binary-field script
Fonts Inter (body/UI), Instrument Sans and Inter Tight (display), loaded in the page head per the header comment

side_effects: No JavaScript in this file. It does declare animations that run forever: hero-charge-sheen 3.2s linear infinite and bit-twinkle 4.5s ease-in-out infinite across 12 staggered spans

body background-image embeds an inline data:image/svg+xml grain texture, width 160 height 160, filter id='n' with feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.85' numOctaves='2' stitchTiles='stitch' and feColorMatrix tinting to 0.75 / 0.82 / 0.95 at alpha 0.035, background-repeat repeat. Comment: 'The same whisper of grain as the Droppy site, inverted for the dark canvas so it lifts rather than dirties.'

.hero__charged-sheen embeds a second inline data:image/svg+xml, width 240 height 64 viewBox 0 0 240 64, four copies of the bolt path 'M12 2 4 30h9l-3 22 12-30h-9z' filled %23ffffff at fill-opacity .6, translated to (20 4), (80 4), (140 4), (200 4), each with scale(1.1)
Selection, drag and long-press are suppressed site-wide; the comment says the scripts back this up by swallowing copy, cut, drag and the context menu
platform_assumptions: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) drives --nav-safe-top: an iOS/iPadOS Safari safe-area concept used to push the fixed nav below a device notch

--font-mono is ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace, an Apple-only stack with no Windows fallback; the header comment says 'Code inside the chips uses the Mac's own SF Mono; nothing else is imported', so on Windows the generic monospace would be used
-webkit-backdrop-filter paired with backdrop-filter on .glass and .btn--darkpill targets WebKit/Safari first
-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%, -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased and -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale; the grayscale smoothing hint is macOS-specific
-webkit-touch-callout: none, -webkit-user-drag: none and -webkit-user-select: none are Safari/iOS specifics used for the anti-copy lockdown
-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch on .showcase-highlights__rail is an iOS Safari momentum-scroll hint, alongside a ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none } rule
border-shape: shape(...) sits behind @supports as progressive enhancement over the two radial-gradient fillet pseudo-elements; it is a very new CSS feature likely only in Safari at the pinned commit
min-height: 100dvh, aspect-ratio, overflow-x: clip, text-wrap: balance / pretty, grid-template-rows 0fr animation and the [inert] attribute selector all require a modern engine
The .hero__apple glyph and the .btn--applepill CTA assume a Mac download is the primary action

feature_notes: Site-wide anti-copy lockdown: body gets -webkit-user-select and user-select none plus -webkit-touch-callout none, and img and video get -webkit-user-drag none and pointer-events none. Comment: 'Nothing on the page is for taking: no text selection, no dragging a picture or a film off the page, no long-press sheet on a phone. The scripts back this up by swallowing copy, cut, drag and the context menu.' A follow-up comment notes the theme picker's names are buttons and the FAQ questions are buttons, so those keep their pointer events; only the media itself is inert.
html gets overflow-x: clip, -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% and scroll-behavior: smooth globally; body gets min-height 100dvh, line-height 1.6 and the grain background.

The nav dock springs open once per visit: the pill runs navDockExpand for 640ms on cubic-bezier(0.32, 1.22, 0.36, 1) after a 120ms delay, starting collapsed at translateY(-6px) scaleX(0.78) with blur(8px), 'like the Droppy shelf (shelf curve + blur snapping into focus)'. A head-inline gate adds html.nav-intro-done on later loads so it never replays when navigating between pages; prefers-reduced-motion also sets animation: none. The comment states the tokens and keyframes are the getdroppy.app ones, unchanged.

The notch fillets are drawn twice: as radial-gradient pseudo-elements by default, and, where the browser supports border-shape: shape(...), as one border-shape path while ::before and ::after get content: none and --notch-fillet-inset becomes var(--notch-fillet) so the padding compensates.

Morph hover is 'the one hover every button on the site shares'. Two stacked content layers (a REST face and a HOVER face) are built at runtime by site.js so button markup stays plain; on hover the label dissolves through a thick gaussian blur where it stands and a fitting glyph blurs in, centred. The comment is emphatic in capitals: 'NOTHING SLIDES AND NOTHING RESIZES: the silhouette is identical at rest and hovered, only the content changes.'

Hover is gated behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) because 'on iOS Safari a synthesised hover would swallow the first tap'; touch gets the same morph from the .is-tapmorph class, which runs the 620ms tap-out and tap-in animations. .btn-morph--icon swaps faces; .btn-morph--label only runs the 340ms dissolve on its rest face.

Under prefers-reduced-motion the morph system removes the hover face entirely (display: none), cancels the label dissolve and both tap animations, keeps the rest face at opacity 1 with filter none, and falls back to .btn-morph:hover { opacity: 0.85 }.

The hero's charged word replays the choreography of 'Supercharged' on getdroppy.app: once the headline's reveal settles (.is-settled) a strike drops into the word from the top of the viewport over 850ms, an arrival bloom pulses once over 900ms, and a sheen keeps sweeping through the letters at 3.2s linear forever. The comment says Droppy's strike is a lightning bolt while here it is a stream of ones and zeros, and the sheen carries a row of digits instead of a bolt, although the embedded sheen SVG still draws four bolt paths.

Before the headline settles, .hero__title:not(.is-settled) hides the sheen, the charge entry and the ::after bloom with display: none; a will-change: opacity, transform compositing hint is held only while the shared reveal runs and is dropped to auto under reduced motion.

The binary field behind the hero is one canvas fixed to the hero's box, masked with linear-gradient(180deg, #000 0%, #000 55%, transparent 100%) 'so it melts into the page before the promo block'. The outro repeats the idea with radial-gradient(60% 70% at 50% 50%, #000 20%, transparent 100%).

Every tour still is a whole 16:10 frame, so .hero__film, .fcard__media, .fcard__media--window, .highlight-card .fcard__media and .wordscroll__demo-video all use aspect-ratio 16 / 10; the comments say a 16:9 or window-shaped box with cover cropped their edges, and .wordscroll__demo-video therefore uses object-fit contain so no bars and no crop.

The highlight rail is a full-bleed (100vw, margin-left calc(50% - 50vw)) horizontally scrolling, mandatory snap-stopped, drag-scrollable carousel with two round arrow buttons that disable at the ends at opacity 0.28 and cursor default; reduced motion turns off smooth scrolling and the arrow transitions.

The tile system is declared as the one card system: 'Every card on the page is a tile: a big-radius well with generous padding, one bold label, and either a large illustration or a visual that is allowed to bleed off the edge. Nothing else lives in a tile: no small icon chips, no key caps, no paragraphs under paragraphs.'

Picture tiles (.tile--fade) keep copy and capture apart: the copy sits at the top and the capture stands under it, running off the bottom and one side and fading out before the edge. Comment: 'Never under the words: the copy keeps its own band, the picture takes what is left.'

The FAQ list reads as a back-and-forth zig-zag: every question is a content-sized pill drawn by a ::before pseudo-element (so the round button can sit outside it on the page canvas and the row still works when a page ships the question as a bare text node), only every second one is pushed right with margin-left auto, and the answer card mirrors to the opposite side with a 28px accent dot in the side margin. Phones take the full-width pill back for both sides and hide the dots.

The FAQ answer opens with the grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr technique over var(--dur-base) 300ms, and the icon swaps its plus svg (hidden via visibility: hidden, so the circle keeps its size) for a 16x2px minus bar while filling with var(--accent).
The free and open-source card explicitly 'takes the pricing slot' and is centred 'as the pricing card on getdroppy.app is'.

The footer wordmark is a giant clipped word at rgba(232, 237, 245, 0.05) inside a fixed-height overflow-hidden box with will-change: transform and transform translateY(0.06em), implying a script-driven parallax translate.

The theme picker is one big window in the chosen theme plus the names to pick from, and lives inside the second wordscroll's demo slot. Its width is min(1040px, 86vw, calc(60vh * 2080 / 1426)) so that the window, its 26 names and the caption all fit the pinned stage together; the stage is at the same 2080 / 1426 aspect ratio.
The .wordscroll__bits binary twinkles are described as replacing Droppy's sparks.

Comments declare the intentional flat look: --border-subtle and --border-strong are transparent tokens kept only so rules can reference them ('Kept as tokens, intentionally invisible: flat look, no outlines'), and --shadow-card is none ('Disabled: flat look, no shadows, no glow effects').
unresolved_questions: Several classes are styled here but their markup lives in website/*.html and their behavior in website/assets/js/*, none of which are in this bundle: the .wordscroll__* mechanism (only __demo-video and __bits are styled here), the .hero__charge-entry inner SVG content, and the theme picker's 26 theme names.

.tile__rows has only a mobile override (margin 8px -28px 0 0 under 620px) and no base rule anywhere in this file, so its default layout must come from elsewhere or the base rule was dropped in the port.

--nav-dock-fade-duration and --nav-dock-exit-curve are declared in the second :root block but never referenced in this file; they may be consumed by site.js or be dead carry-over from getdroppy.app, and that cannot be decided from CSS alone.

Declared but unused in this file: --radius-2xl, --accent-hover, --accent-active, --accent-glow, --color-error, --color-warning, --surface-dark, --glass-border, --glass-border-strong, --shadow-card, --bg-bottom, --text-3xl, --text-4xl, --text-5xl, --text-6xl. Whether another stylesheet or script reads them is not determinable from this bundle.

.outro__icon-wrap::before is explicitly set to content: none, which suggests it cancels a glow from the upstream Droppy sheet; the original rule is not present here, so the intended appearance it removes cannot be recovered.

The header comment says the fonts are loaded in the page head, so the exact <link> or @font-face declarations are in the HTML, not this file. Notably "Inter Tight" is named first in many rules but is not part of --font-display, so whether it is actually requested cannot be confirmed here.

purpose: Stylesheet for the marketing site's pinned 'wordscroll' section: a 500vh tall dark slab whose sticky stage cross-fades scroll-lit headline copy into a product demo video, driven entirely by CSS custom properties that wordscroll.js writes. Carries three layouts in one file: a static no-JS base, the .ws-ready pinned treatment, and a .ws-reduced-motion fallback.
calls_into: CSS custom properties written by website/assets/js/wordscroll.js: --ws-enter, --ws-glow, --ws-copy, --ws-demo, --ws-bloom (also --ws-media and --ws-field-shift in split layout, declared only by the JS)
site.css variables: var(--ink), var(--border-subtle), var(--text-primary), var(--font-display)
Classes toggled by JS: .ws-ready, .ws-reduced-motion, .ws-demo-active, and word spans .w / .w-dim / .w-lit / .w-glo created by wordscroll.js
state_owned: Stage-local custom property defaults declared on .wordscroll__stage: --ws-enter: 1, --ws-glow: 0.6, --ws-copy: 1, --ws-demo: 1, --ws-bloom: 0
Pinned overrides on .wordscroll.ws-ready .wordscroll__stage: --ws-enter: 0, --ws-glow: 0, --ws-copy: 1, --ws-demo: 0, --ws-bloom: 0
Reduced-motion overrides: --ws-enter: 1, --ws-copy: 1, --ws-demo: 1, --ws-glow: 0.6
side_effects: Runs the infinite CSS animation ws-twinkle (4.5s ease-in-out infinite) on ten spark dots; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
platform_assumptions: Assumes modern browser support for position: sticky, 100dvh, overflow-x: clip, aspect-ratio, clamp(), vmax units and CSS custom properties in calc()
Not macOS-specific; it is plain web CSS for the product site and has no AppKit/SwiftUI dependency

formatDate only rewrites a strict /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/ string, builds a local Date(year, month-1, day) to avoid a timezone day shift, and renders it as en-US { month: 'long', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' } (so "2026-07-06" -> "July 6, 2026"); anything else is passed through unchanged, and a non-string returns ""
Sorting is numeric per dot-separated segment with missing or NaN segments treated as 0, newest first, on a copy of the array (slice) so the fetched data is not mutated
Every entry is drawn as a stable release: the code comments say every entry on this page wears the one blue pill with the droplet glyph and the Stable label; release.platform is never read
Thanks strings are split on /@([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)/g and each captured handle becomes an <a class="changelog-thanks__handle"> with text "@handle" pointing at https://gitlab.com/<handle>
Reveal observer uses rootMargin "0px 0px -5% 0px" and threshold 0 (deliberately, so very long release cards reveal as soon as they start entering the viewport) and unobserves each card once revealed
The floating icon picks its host slot by the entry whose rect straddles a line at 42% of the viewport height (vh * 0.42), otherwise the nearest entry by distance to that line

The hand-off is a FLIP glide: measure, reparent, then transform translate3d(dx,dy,0) with transition "transform 640ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1)" back to zero, re-armed after 680ms; under prefers-reduced-motion the icon reparents with no animation
initEntryIcon bails if there are no islots or a .clog-float-icon already exists, so the icon is created exactly once
Entries that are not objects are skipped; if nothing renders, the empty state shows

The trail digit is computed from position, not the seeded cell: ((r*7 + c*13 + yi) & 1) ? '1' : '0', so the streaming head shows a deterministic pattern while resting cells keep their seeded bit

The cycle only runs while the picker is at least 40% visible and stops when it leaves; it is never started under prefers-reduced-motion

purpose: Shared script for every page of the marketing site, in two IIFEs. The first owns reveal-on-load/reveal-on-scroll, the FAQ accordion, the injected skip link, the phone notch menu, the active nav link, the footer year, the footer wordmark parallax and an anti-copy guard. The second builds the button 'morph hover' DOM: it wraps each button's children in a rest face and adds a hover face carrying a glyph, chosen from data-morph-glyph, a leading icon child, or a label regex table.

Word sweep window: startProgress 0.10 (0.08 in split layout), endProgress 0.40 (0.66 in split layout); per-word span = (end - start) / count * 2.4
Per-word transform while lighting: translateY of 0.12 * (1-value)^2 - 0.04 * sin(PI * value) em, to 4 decimals; cleared to "" once value reaches 1
--ws-copy = 1 - clamp((progress - 0.47) / 0.08, 0, 1) (constant 1 in split layout)
--ws-demo = clamp((progress - 0.52) / 0.08, 0, 1) (constant 1 in split layout)
--ws-bloom = clamp(1 - |progress - 0.53| / 0.11, 0, 1); split layout uses clamp(1 - |progress - 0.48| / 0.42, 0, 1)
Split layout also writes --ws-media = progress and --ws-field-shift = (progress - 0.5) * 9
Glow word highlight: peak at (its lit point + 0.02) with a half-width of 0.05, i.e. clamp(1 - |progress - (highlightLit + 0.02)| / 0.05, 0, 1)

Drifting marks (split layout): grouped six at a time with group starts [0, 0.18, 0.36, 0.56], peak = start + 0.16, end = min(1, start + 0.4); opacity = phase * (0.5 + (index % 4) * 0.08) to 3 decimals; transform translate3d(direction * (progress - peak) * 5 px, -direction * (progress - peak) * 7 px, 0) scale(0.92 + phase * 0.08), direction alternating by index parity
Preload threshold: progress > 0.25 (0.02 in split layout); play threshold: progress > 0.5 (0.1 in split layout)
IntersectionObserver rootMargin "20% 0px"
Property write epsilon: values are only written when they differ by more than 0.001
feature_notes: Progress is computed from the section rect: clamp(-rect.top / (rect.height - window.innerHeight)); if that denominator is <= 0 the update bails, so an unpinned section never scrubs

The demo slot may be the video itself (homepage shelf demo) or a card that wraps a video (creators page), and several such cards may exist; the section owns play/pause for every media element so an off-screen stage never decodes frames

Under prefers-reduced-motion the section still gets .ws-ready but also .ws-reduced-motion, demo.inert is set false, every video gains a controls attribute, and the function returns before any scroll wiring, so nothing scrubs
In the non-split layout .ws-demo-active is only added once --ws-demo reaches 0.99, gating pointer events on the demo; in split layout the demo is always active
Videos swap to their data-remote source only off localhost/127.0.0.1, keeping local development on the local file
Pausing is driven both by scroll progress and by IntersectionObserver leaving and by document.hidden, so a hidden tab stops playback
The re-entrancy guard __droppyWordscroll means a section is only initialized once even if the script runs twice
The legacy .social-benchmark__infinities span selector is kept only so the social license page keeps working; new pages opt in with [data-wordscroll-marks]
unresolved_questions: The 'glow' variable computed as sweep is written to --ws-glow but no rule in wordscroll.css reads it; its visual effect must come from another stylesheet not in this bundle

The entry-lookup loop that walks hlEntries backwards duplicates the push that immediately precedes it, so a second, independent path to attach a .w-glo span exists; whether it can ever match a different entry than the one just pushed is not determinable from this file alone
data-wordscroll-split pages (the creators / social license pages) are not in this bundle, so the split-layout mark markup and its stylesheet could not be confirmed
